title: What is compliance training?
description: Compliance training defined: how it links to legal and voluntary obligations, what ISO 37301 expects, and how it differs from mandatory training.
shortAnswer: Compliance training is structured workplace learning that equips people to meet the laws, regulations, licence conditions, standards and internal policies that apply to their role. Under ISO 37301, the international compliance management standard, it is one control within a wider compliance management system, and it should be traceable to identified compliance obligations and assessed compliance risks rather than chosen as a list of generic topics.
keyTakeaways: Compliance training exists to help an organisation meet its compliance obligations: the requirements it must meet and those it chooses to meet.
ISO 37301 treats training (clause 7.2.3) and awareness (clause 7.3) as separate support requirements within a compliance management system.
Good compliance training is traceable: obligation, role, learning outcome, assessment and record line up.

Australian law often requires training outcomes without prescribing a course, for example the WHS duty to provide necessary training and the AFS licensee duty to keep representatives adequately trained.
Completion records show attendance. Regulators and auditors increasingly look for evidence that people can apply the requirement.

blocks.text: Compliance training is learning designed so that people know, understand and can apply the requirements that govern their work. Its purpose is narrower than general professional development: it exists because an obligation exists, and it should change behaviour in the situations where that obligation applies.

The term is anchored by [ISO 37301:2021](https://www.iso.org/standard/75080.html), the certifiable international standard for compliance management systems published in April 2021. ISO 37301 defines compliance obligations as requirements an organisation "mandatorily has to comply with as well as those that an organization voluntarily chooses to comply with". Compliance training therefore covers legislation and regulator rules, and also codes, contracts and internal policies the organisation has adopted. The obligations themselves are usually listed in a [compliance obligations register](/glossary/compliance-obligations-register).

The ISO technical committee's [published FAQ](https://committee.iso.org/files/live/sites/tc309/files/FAQ%2037301/ISO%2037301%20FAQs,%20May%202022.pdf) lists "personnel trainings and communications" among the measures the standard requires, alongside identifying obligations, assessing compliance risk, monitoring and corrective action. Training is one control, not the whole system.

sections.heading: How does compliance training work in practice?

blocks.text: Effective compliance training runs as a cycle that starts from obligations, not from content. The steps below reflect the sequence implied by ISO 37301 and by Australian regulator guidance.

items: **Identify obligations.** List the legal, regulatory and voluntary requirements that apply, and keep the list current when rules change.
**Assess risk and exposure by role.** Decide which roles face which obligations and how serious a breach would be.
**Define learning outcomes.** Write what a person must be able to do, not only what they must read. See [learning outcomes](/glossary/learning-outcomes).
**Design and deliver.** Choose formats that fit the risk: short e-learning for awareness, supervised practice for high risk tasks.
**Assess and record.** Check understanding or competence and keep records that link each person to the obligation and version of the material.
**Review.** Refresh on a defined cycle and whenever an obligation, process or risk changes.

blocks.text: Australian law usually sets the outcome rather than the course. Section 19(3)(f) of the Work Health and Safety Act 2011 requires a person conducting a business or undertaking to ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, "the provision of any information, training, instruction or supervision that is necessary to protect all persons" from work risks, as [Comcare's regulatory guide](https://www.comcare.gov.au/scheme-legislation/whs-act/regulatory-guides/primary-duty-of-care) sets out. For financial services, the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) notes in [RG 105](https://asic.gov.au/regulatory-resources/find-a-document/regulatory-guides/rg-105-afs-licensing-organisational-competence/) that s912A(1)(f) of the Corporations Act requires licensees to ensure representatives are trained and competent.

sections.heading: How is compliance training different from related terms?

blocks.text: Compliance training overlaps with several terms that are often used interchangeably but mean different things.

blocks.caption: Compliance training and neighbouring terms
head: Term
What it means
Relationship to compliance training
rows: [Mandatory training](/glossary/mandatory-training)
Training the organisation requires people to complete, whether or not a law demands it
Most compliance training is mandatory, but some mandatory training (for example, a new system rollout) is not about compliance
Awareness
Knowing that a policy or obligation exists and why it matters (ISO 37301 clause 7.3)
A lower bar than training; often delivered by communication rather than instruction
[Policy attestation](/glossary/policy-attestation)
A signed or recorded statement that a person has read and will follow a policy
Evidence of acknowledgement, not of understanding or competence
[Competency assessment](/glossary/competency-assessment)
Judging whether a person can perform to a standard
The strongest evidence that compliance training worked

blocks.text: The practical difference between completion and competence is explored in [completion tracking vs competency verification](/compare/completion-tracking-vs-competency-verification).

sections.heading: What does traceable compliance training look like?

blocks.text: The table below is an **illustrative example** for a whistleblower obligation in an Australian public company. ASIC's [RG 270](https://asic.gov.au/regulatory-resources/find-a-document/regulatory-guides/rg-270-whistleblower-policies/) says an entity should conduct upfront and ongoing training on its whistleblower policy for every employee, with specialist training for staff who receive disclosures (RG 270.131 and RG 270.134).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records each obligation, the concepts a person needs, and the assessment points that prove understanding before any training content is written. Each learning outcome then carries a link back to its source obligation, so the mapping in the example above is held as data rather than rebuilt for each audit.

faqs.q: Is compliance training required by law in Australia?
faqs.a: Often, but rarely as a named course. Laws such as the WHS Act and the Corporations Act require training or competence as an outcome. Regulator guides then explain expectations. Some roles also need specific licences or accredited training. Organisations decide the format, and must be able to show the outcome was achieved.

Yes, for organisations that adopt the standard. It includes requirements for competence, training and awareness within the support clauses. ISO 37301 is voluntary, but it can become a contractual or procurement requirement, and certification by an independent body is available because it is a requirements standard.

faqs.q: How often should compliance training be refreshed?
faqs.a: There is no single rule. Refresh cycles should follow the obligation, the risk and any regulator expectation, and training should also be updated whenever the underlying requirement changes. A fixed annual cycle alone can leave content out of date between reviews. See the guide on setting mandatory training refresh cycles.

faqs.q: Is a completion certificate enough evidence?
faqs.a: Completion proves that someone finished a module. It does not show that they understood or can apply the requirement. For higher risk obligations, regulators and auditors look for assessment results, supervisor sign off or verification of competency linked to the version of the material used.

factCheck.claim: ISO 37301 was published in April 2021, is edition 1, has Amendment 1:2024 and was reviewed and confirmed in 2026.

ISO 37301 clause 3.25 defines compliance obligations as requirements an organization mandatorily has to comply with as well as those it voluntarily chooses to comply with; clause 7.2.3 is Training and 7.3 is Awareness.
ISO TC 309 FAQ lists personnel trainings and communications among what ISO 37301 requires, and states it is a requirements standard capable of certification.
WHS Act s19(3)(f) requires provision of any information, training, instruction or supervision necessary to protect all persons from risks arising from work.
RG 105.3 notes s912A(1)(f) obligation to ensure representatives are trained and competent.
RG 270.131 says entities should conduct upfront and ongoing training on the whistleblower policy for every employee; RG 270.134 says specialist training for staff with specific responsibilities.
